questions.question: 100% of this IPO's money is an offer for sale. Where does that part of the money go?

choices.text: Into the company, to build new factories.
To the existing owners who are selling their shares.

questions.explanation: In an offer for sale, existing owners sell shares they already hold, so the money goes to them. Only the fresh issue, ₹0 crore here, reaches EAAA India Alternatives Limited.

questions.explanation: 32.9% a year is healthy growth: EAAA India Alternatives Limited's customers are buying more each year.

questions.question: EAAA India Alternatives Limited owes 0.41 rupees of loans for every rupee of its owners' money. Which is closest to the truth?

choices.text: Its loans are small to manageable next to what the owners have put in.
Its loans are heavy: lenders have more riding on it than its owners.
Loans never matter for a company that makes a profit.

questions.explanation: At 0.41 rupees of loans per rupee of owners' money, EAAA India Alternatives Limited's owners have more in the business than its lenders.

numbers.label: Loans for every rupee of owners' money

questions.question: Big institutions asked for 13.1x the shares kept for them. Why do people watch this figure?

choices.text: Professionals who studied the company closely are showing how keen they are.
It guarantees the share price will rise on listing day.
It tells you how many shares you will be given.

questions.explanation: Institutions do the most homework, and they asked for 13.1x their quota of EAAA India Alternatives Limited: strong appetite. Still, no figure guarantees a listing gain.
